preconditions.description: Attacker must be the contract owner (or gain control of owner account)
Attacker needs some tokens to perform a trade that will incur high fees

violation_target.exploit_hint: As the contract owner, call setBuyTaxes() or setSelTaxes() with extremely high fee percentages (e.g., 99% each). Then perform a token swap through the DEX pair to trigger fee collection. The high fees will be collected in the contract and can be withdrawn to marketing/team wallets (which the owner controls) or through swapAndLiquify mechanism that sends BNB to owner-controlled addresses.

attempts.vulnerability_analysis: The TokenTool contract allows the owner to set extremely high buy/sell taxes (up to 100% total). When users trade through the DEX pair, fees are collected as tokens in the contract, then automatically swapped to BNB and distributed to marketing and team wallets. The owner controls these wallet addresses and can set them to any address, including the attacker's address. By setting 99% fees and controlling the fee recipient addresses, the attacker can siphon funds from traders.
attempts.attack_strategy: 1. Impersonate the contract owner using vm.prank. 2. Set buy and sell taxes to 33% each for liquidity, marketing, and team (99% total). 3. Set marketing and team wallet addresses to the attacker's address. 4. Acquire some tokens to trade. 5. Perform a swap through the DEX pair to trigger the fee mechanism. 6. The 99% fee will be collected, swapped to BNB, and sent to the attacker-controlled wallets.
attempts.step_by_step_plan: 1. Use vm.startPrank() to impersonate the owner. 2. Call setBuyTaxes(33, 33, 33) for 99% buy tax. 3. Call setSelTaxes(33, 33, 33) for 99% sell tax. 4. Call setMarketingWalletAddress(attacker) and setTeamWalletAddress(attacker). 5. Stop prank and get tokens from owner (or use deal if we can manipulate balances). 6. Approve router to spend tokens. 7. Perform swapExactTokensForETHSupportingFeeOnTransferTokens to trigger fee collection. 8. The contract will collect 99% as fee, swap to BNB, and send to attacker.

attempts.vulnerability_analysis: Same as before - owner can set high fees and control fee recipient addresses to siphon funds.
attempts.attack_strategy: 1. Impersonate owner to set high taxes and change fee recipient addresses. 2. Use deal() cheatcode to give tokens directly to attacker. 3. Perform a swap to trigger fee collection. 4. Profit from fee distribution to attacker-controlled addresses.
attempts.step_by_step_plan: 1. Get owner address. 2. Impersonate owner to set 99% taxes. 3. Set marketing and team wallets to attacker address. 4. Use deal() to give attacker a substantial token balance. 5. Approve router. 6. Perform swap to trigger fees. 7. Attacker receives BNB from fee distribution.
attempts.failure_reflection: The previous PoC failed because the owner had zero token balance. The assumption that the owner still holds tokens after deployment was incorrect. In a live contract, tokens may have been distributed, sold, or transferred elsewhere. We need to ensure the attacker has tokens to trade without relying on the owner's balance.
